findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false via convoluted dead logic with no explanation
findings.body: The new helper `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false on every branch — the variable and the `if` are dead code and the function always returns false. That is presumably the intent (hard-disable SQL expressions for the CVE-2024-9264 fix), but nothing in the code says so. The double negative reads like a bug, and a future maintainer may 'fix' it to `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`, silently re-enabling the SQL/DuckDB execution path that was disabled for security reasons. The function should be a plain `return false` with a comment stating the feature is intentionally disabled, or the flag should be checked with an explicit blocklist comment.

findings.title: User-facing error says 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' although the feature exists but is deliberately disabled
findings.body: When a user submits an SQL expression query, ReadQuery now rejects it with the error `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. This is misleading: the feature is implemented but has been disabled for security reasons (CVE-2024-9264). Users who had the sqlExpressions feature flag enabled will see a message implying their Grafana build lacks the feature rather than that it was turned off, which will generate confusing support tickets. The message should state that SQL expressions are disabled/unavailable.

findings.title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path is only blocked implicitly by the stubbed DB erroring out
findings.body: The explicit disable check was added only in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery (pkg/expr/reader.go). The legacy parsing path, UnmarshalSQLCommand, has no feature-flag or disabled check; SQL execution through it is prevented only because NewSQLCommand calls sql.TablesList, which now fails because the stubbed DB.RunCommands returns 'not implemented'. If the stub in pkg/expr/sql/db.go is later replaced with a real implementation (the file keeps the full go-duck API surface, suggesting it is meant to be swapped back), the legacy path would execute SQL with no gate at all. An explicit rejection (mirroring the reader.go check, or an error in NewSQLCommand itself) should guard this path so the security fix does not depend on an incidental error from a stub.

findings.title: No regression test verifies SQL expressions are rejected after the security fix
findings.body: This PR disables SQL expressions to remediate an RCE/LFI vulnerability (CVE-2024-9264), but adds no test asserting the new behavior: e.g. that ReadQuery returns an error for QueryTypeSQL even when the sqlExpressions feature flag is enabled, and that NewSQLCommand/sql.TablesList fail. Without such a test, a future change that restores the go-duck dependency or 'fixes' the always-false enableSqlExpressions helper would re-open the vulnerability without any CI signal.
